On the 1938 map, Yemen (UK) is southern Yemen under Britain: the port of Aden and the sultanates behind it.

Aden was taken in 1839 and for nearly a century was run from British India, as a fueling stop on the way there. In 1937 it became a Crown colony ruled from London. The interior was a patchwork of sultanates and sheikhdoms tied to Britain by treaty, from the hills near Aden to the Hadhramaut valley in the east; see British protectorates in southern Arabia.

To the north lay the Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen, ruled by Zaydi imams, which claimed the south and clashed with Britain on the border. After a rising in the 1960s, Britain left in 1967. The south became a Marxist state, and joined the north as Yemen in 1990.
sum: On the 1938 map, Yemen (UK) is southern Yemen under Britain: the port of Aden and the sultanates behind it.
